title: Regional GPU heatmap-driven drain playbook (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for performing maintenance drains and GPU driver rollouts using a region-by-region heatmap approach. The goal is to minimize customer-impact token-cost and tail-latency regressions while enabling faster driver patching across the global fleet.

Scope:
- Applies to all NVIDIA (A100/H100) pools managed by the infra GPU controller in hosted + dedicated regions.
- Covers: planned maintenance windows, soft-drain mechanics, hard-drain escalation, driver canaries, regional buffer targets, and post-drain verification.
- Excludes emergency incident evacuations (see SRE runbooks).

Summary:
We use a utilization heatmap (7d rolling) that blends: p99 latency headroom, average GPU util %, queue depth, and recent error-rate bump. Heatmap buckets determine how aggressive a drain can be for a given AZ/region on any day. Lower-risk tiles => larger drain slices.

Heatmap inputs (what the script consumes):
- 7d rolling GPU util (avg) per AZ
- 95th token latency headroom (ms) per fleet group
- Active capacity commitments (reserved instances) per customer tier
- Recent model hot-spotting (top-10 models by tokens/s)
- Error-rate delta (last 24h vs baseline)

Drain policy (high level):
- Tile A (green): util < 55% and headroom > 35ms => up to 30% of GPUs can be soft-drained during window
- Tile B (amber): util 55-75% or headroom 15-35ms => up to 15% soft-drain
- Tile C (red): util > 75% or headroom < 15ms => only 5% soft-drain, prefer night windows or postpone

Soft-drain vs hard-drain:
- Soft-drain: mark nodes cordoned, allow existing sessions/KV cache to finish, gracefully stop scheduling new sessions. Target: zero active sessions in 10-30 min depending on average session length.
- Hard-drain: forcibly kill workloads after grace period, used for driver A/B rollback or urgent maintenance. Requires SRE approval and communication.

Regional window examples (text table):
- US-WEST: preferred window 02:00-06:00 PDT (weekday early morning), baseline buffer 20%
- EU-CENTRAL: 01:00-05:00 CET (Thu-Fri), buffer 25%
- APAC-SOUTH: 00:00-04:00 IST (Sun-Mon), buffer 30%

Buffer rules:
- Buffer = min(allocated_capacity * buffer_pct, absolute_min_pool_gpus)
- Default absolute_min_pool_gpus = 40 GPUs per region for production pools
- If reserved commitments would violate buffer, schedule maintenance in dedicated-only pools first

Driver rollout plan (canary + phased):
1) Canary cluster (single AZ, non-critical pool): deploy driver package, run smoke + long-context perf test harness (10k tokens each) for 2h. Check diff: tail latency, CPU utilization, kernel errors.
2) Canary-AZ (1-2 AZs behind heatmap green tiles): drain 5% soft, apply driver, monitor 4h. If regression > 10% p95 latency or new CUDA errors, revert.
3) Regional phased (per heatmap buckets): apply in slices as allowed by policy above, monitor 12h between slices.
4) Global cohort (low-traffic regions first) then higher-traffic after 48h of clean telemetry.

Telemetry and gates (automated):
- Gate 1 (smoke): container start success > 99% for 30m
- Gate 2 (latency): p95 token latency not increased by > 10% relative to 24h baseline for 2h
- Gate 3 (errors): new driver kernel errors = 0 for 60m, otherwise fail
- Gate 4 (cost): average token compute time within expected bounds otherwise investigate

Automations we rely on (ops notes):
- heatmap-generator lambda -> pushes bucket decisions to ops-cache
- drain-controller orchestrates soft drain and monitors session count
- canary-deployer handles driver install and rollback hooks
- routing-policy-service will automatically move requests to fallback model variants if p99 latency crosses 250ms (configurable)

Runbook (quick checklist) - pre-maintenance:
- Notify slack: #infra-maintenance and on-call 72h, 24h, 2h
- Verify capacity commitments (billing/committed pools) and pause auto-scale rules that would fight drain
- Snapshot kernel logs for baseline (nvml, dmesg)
- Ensure SRE and Platform on-call are assigned
- Create ephemeral alert suppression for non-actionable noise (list IDs)

Runbook (during):
- Kick off heatmap job and confirm tile states
- Start soft-drain for slice-1 in region X (document node ids)
- Watch sessions drop to 0 or expected baseline, if not, extend grace period by +15m
- Apply driver to slice-1 via canary-deployer
- Wait for Gate 1-3 duration and confirm
- If green, proceed to slice-2; if not, revert and file post-mortem

Rollback criteria (immediate revert):
- Kernel OOMs or driver panics reported on >1 node within 10m
- p95 token latency regression > 20% or p99 > 30% sustained for 15m
- Any increase in user-facing error rate (5xx) by >0.5% absolute

Post-maintenance verification:
- 24h perf summary: p50/p95/p99, GPU util, queue depth, error rates
- Confirm KV cache hit-rate not degraded by >3%
- Billing check: expected token-hours vs actual < 5% variance
- Small targeted synthetic tests across top-10 customers (run evals)

Edge cases / notes to self (informal):
- If heatmap is stale (data lag > 10m) treat region as amber by default
- For Dedicated customers with SLA locks, route maintenance to minor windows only; coordinate 2 weeks ahead
- Some older pools still on legacy cuda-11 stacks — special path required (see linked PR)
- Manual evictions can cause cache fragmentation leading to short-term perf blips (monitor KV-cache evict metrics)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide SLO change window for driver rollouts affecting p99-sensitive customers (cc: product-hosted-api)
- Add synthetic load generator that mimics largest model spiky traffic for canary tests (diego owning)
- Document step-by-step rollback automation in a separate runbook (Marcus to draft)

Appendix: quick commands (examples)
- Generate heatmap (dev): ./scripts/heatmap --window=7d --region=us-west
- Trigger soft-drain: ./opsctl drain --region eu-central --percent 10 --grace 20m
- Install driver canary: ./canaryctl apply --driver v530.41 --pool=canary-us-west

Slack channels / contacts:
- #infra-maintenance (broadcast)
- #sre-oncall (escalation)
- Primary on-call: Marcus Chen
- Secondary: Eleni Vassiliou

Logs / artifacts to capture after each slice: node-ids.txt, nvml_dump.tgz, perf-summary.json, canary-deployer.log

-- end of working draft --
(Notes: still needs a short post-mortem template and a heatmap visualization with color thresholds. Move to in_review once those are added and Diego verifies canary harness.)
